messages:
maria: quick heads-up, ran a short nsys capture to investigate the KV-affinity perf regression we saw on canary. got weird kernel hop spikes ~2.3s into the request. using a focused short-run since we only wanted the hot window.

sam: can you paste the exact command you used? were you doing bracketed nvtx capture or full-run?

maria: pasted the command — used nvtx markers and a short duration to avoid massive qdrep files:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --output=~/traces/kv_affinity_short.qdrep \
  --duration=8 \
  --sample=cpu \
  --force-overwrite \
  --capture-range=nvtx
```

maria: notes: I placed NVTX push/pop around the KV lookup + decode path. the timeline shows multiple kernel switches: small preprocessing kernel -> big `kv_decode` -> tiny memcpy -> another kernel that looks like quantize/transpose. the spikes align with KV cache evictions (see nvtx markers).

lee: short capture is fine but beware of sampling bias — if your sample window cuts a long-running kernel it can undercount tail time. If you're trying to correlate evictions use bracketed capture (nvtx markers) like you did, but increase duration or capture one extra second of warmdown.

aj: two quick tips: 1) in the GPU Kernels lane, group by name and sort by total time, then filter to `kv_*` kernels — that'll show which kernel is dominating. 2) enable the "API Trace" and look at CUDA memcpy / async calls: sometimes a stream sync causes serialization that looks like kernel switching.

perf-bot: perf/regression: staging p95 latency +12% vs baseline on same commit (automated trace link: https://perf.internal/traces/kv_affinity_short) :warning:

sam: also try capturing OSRT markers (you already did) and then in nsys timeline toggle the OSRT/CPU sampling view. sampling frequency matters — if you used the default it might be sparse. For tiny windows, prefer bracketed NVTX + `--duration` long enough to capture two full requests.

maria: good call. i'll re-run with 12s and add 1s warmdown, and turn off CPU sampling (`--sample=none`) to reduce noise, then attach the qdrep. also will add an extra NVTX tag before/after KV eviction to narrow it down.

lee: last thing — check the "Device Activity > SM Utilization" and the kernel occupancy column. Low occupancy + long runtime often points to memory stalls (KV decode is memory-heavy). if you see repeated small kernel launches, that can be the batching heuristic firing too often.

maria: thanks all — re-running now. will drop the trace in #eng-runtime and ping @sam once uploaded. :thumbsup:
